senses.gloss: (b. h.; denom. of מֶלַח)to salt, brine; esp. (in ritual law) to strew salt on raw meat to resorb its blood.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Middot 5:3">Midd. V, 3</cite> <he>היו מוֹלְחִין עורות וכ׳</he> they put salt on the hides of sacrifices.—
<cite ref="Chullin 113a:10">Ḥull. 113ᵃ</cite> <he>אלא א״כ מוֹלְחוֹ יפה יפה וכ׳</he> unless one salts it carefully and washes it thoroughly.
<cite ref="Chullin 113a:10">Ib.</cite> <he>מדיח ומוֹלֵחַ וכ׳</he> one must first wash the meat, then salt it and again wash it.

<cite ref="Bava Batra 74b:6">B. Bath. 74ᵇ</cite> <he>ומְלָחָהּ לצדיקים וכ׳</he> and preserved it in salt for the benefit of the righteous &c. Ḥull. l. c. <he>דג טהור שמְלָחוֹ וכ׳</he> a clean fish which was salted together with an unclean one; a. fr.—Part. pass. <cite ref="M01505"><he>מָלוּחַ</he></cite> (v. <cite ref="M01552"><he>מְלִיחַ</he></cite>); pl. <he>מְלוּחִים</he>, <he>מְלוּחִין</he>. Ib. <he>שניהם מ׳</he> both were salted, opp. <cite ref="V00827"><he>תָּפֵל</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 887">Yalk. Ps. 887</cite> <he>מ׳</he> salty secretions.—
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 4:5:19">Y. Taan. IV, 69ᵇ</cite> top <he>מיני מ׳</he> various kinds of salted food.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 1:4:5">Y. Sabb. I, 3ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>מְלוּחֵיהֶן</he> brines prepared by gentiles; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to be strewn with salt. Sifra Vayikra, N’dab., Par. 9, ch. XI שלא הוּמְלְחָה no salt had been put on it.

units: <cite ref="Kiddushin 29b:11">Kidd. 29ᵇ</cite> <he>אם היה בנו זריז וממ׳</he> (Var. <he>וממולא</he>) if his son is eager to learn and bright; [our w. missing in <cite ref="Tosefta Bekhorot 6:10">Tosef. Bekh. VI, 10</cite>).
